memory_bandwidth.notes: Block has many sequential ops (LN, qkv, attn, proj, residual, LN, fc1, gelu, fc2, residual). Each unfused op roundtrips through HBM. Working set per pixel is tiny (32 ch fp16 = 64B). Total tensor ~57MB.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Memory-bound overall; fusion is key. Weight matrices: qkv(32x96=6KB), proj(32x32=2KB), fc1(32x128=8KB), fc2(128x32=8KB) all fit in shared mem easily.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window working set: N=16 tokens × C=32 = 512 fp16 = 1KB. Hidden activations 16×128=4KB. All weights together ~24KB fp16. Fits comfortably in shared memory of a CTA.
register_pressure.risk: Full-fusion feasible per window in shared memory.

nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Swin block (LN->WMSA(W=4x4,h=1,C=32)->residual->LN->MLP(ratio=4)->residual). Input 1x720x1280x32 fp16. Windows: 180x320=57600 windows, each N=16 tokens. DIMS: C=32 small, hidden=128 small, N=16 small => all matmuls are tiny per window. LAYOUT: input (B,H,W,C) contig; window partition is a reshape+permute. WEIGHTS small (~24KB total fp16): qkv 32->96, proj 32->32, fc1 32->128, fc2 128->32; rpe_bias (1,1,16,16). BOTTLENECKS by regime: (a) full eager => HBM roundtrip per op dominates (memory-bound). (b) torch.compile fused => still likely several kernels; LN+matmul fusion limited. (c) custom single-kernel per window => compute could become limiter for the 4 GEMMs but tiny K=32 still underutilizes TC. STRATEGY: FULL FUSION — one kernel processes a batch of windows; load weights once into shared mem (or even constants), do LN1 (reduce over C=32), qkv, attn (N x N = 16x16), softmax+rpe, proj, residual, LN2, fc1+GELU, fc2, residual, store. Window partition can be done implicitly by computing source indices. Multiple windows per program improve TC utilization (e.g., BLOCK_W windows -> effective M=BLOCK_W*N for matmuls). KEY OPS in canonical form: For each window w (size 4x4=16 tokens, 32 ch): x_in = input gather; y1 = LN(x_in); qkv = y1 @ Wqkv + bqkv; q,k,v split; a = softmax(q@k^T/sqrt(C) + rpe); h = a@v @ Wproj + bproj + x_in; y2 = LN(h); m = GELU(y2@Wfc1+b1) @ Wfc2 + b2; out = h + m. CONSTRAINTS: fp16 IO, fp32 accumulate for LN and matmul. OPEN ACTIONS: (1) single fused triton kernel per group-of-windows; (2) fused LN+QKV+attn kernel then fused proj+residual+LN2+MLP kernel; (3) keep PyTorch for window partition but fuse MLP block. SELF_CHECK families differ in fusion granularity — mutually exclusive top-level strategies.

action.description: Write a single Triton kernel that, per program, processes a batch of BLOCK_W windows (each N=16 tokens, C=32). Load all weights (qkv, proj, fc1, fc2, biases, rpe, LN gammas/betas) into registers/shared once per program. Inside the kernel perform: gather input window, LN1, qkv via tl.dot, attention with softmax+rpe, attn@v, proj, add residual, LN2, fc1+GELU, fc2, add residual, scatter to output. Use fp32 accumulators for LN and matmuls, fp16 storage.
action.rationale: Full fusion eliminates ~10 HBM roundtrips. Weight set ~24KB fits in shared memory. Multiple windows per program (e.g., 8 or 16) increases effective M for tl.dot so tensor cores are usefully utilized despite tiny K=32.
action.title: Fully fused per-window-batch Triton kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: tl.dot on Blackwell wants M,N>=16 and K multiple of 16; C=32 K is ok; with BLOCK_W*N = 8*16=128 M dim, fc1 becomes 128x32 @ 32x128, decent.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Batching windows raises arithmetic intensity per kernel launch.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Register/shared pressure if BLOCK_W too large; softmax over N=16 trivial.

memory_bandwidth.risk: Need to verify gather pattern for window partition stays coalesced.

register_pressure.risk: Spilling if BLOCK_W too large; tune to 2-8.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: This is a top-level alternative — incompatible with splitting attention vs MLP across kernels. Top priority because weight set easily fits and memory-bound block benefits most from fusion.

action.description: Two Triton kernels: K1 fuses LN1 + QKV + attention(softmax+rpe) + attn@v + proj + residual1; K2 fuses LN2 + fc1 + GELU + fc2 + residual2. Each kernel processes batches of windows / token-rows. Avoids the worst register pressure of full fusion while still eliminating most HBM roundtrips.
action.rationale: Slightly easier to implement than full fusion; still ~1 HBM roundtrip vs ~10 for eager. The intermediate (B,H,W,C) tensor between K1 and K2 is small (57MB) and can stay in HBM cheaply.
action.title: Two-kernel split: attention-block + MLP-block

action.description: Implement an MLP-only fused kernel (LN2 + fc1 + GELU + fc2 + residual) since the MLP path is heaviest (hidden=128). Use PyTorch (or simple Triton) for the attention path. Easier and lower-risk first step; gives a quick performance baseline and validates Triton tooling.
action.rationale: MLP dominates FLOPs (32->128->32 vs 32->96 + 16x16 attn). Fusing LN+matmul+GELU+matmul+residual removes 4 HBM roundtrips on the largest activations. Low risk warm-up implementation.
action.title: MLP-only fused Triton kernel (warm-up)

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin block (single head, no shift, window 4x4, dim=32, mlp_ratio=4) on a 1x720x1280x32 fp16 input. Composed of LN1, QKV linear, scaled dot-product attention with relative position bias over N=16 tokens, output projection + residual, LN2, MLP (32->128->32 with GELU) + residual. All weight matrices are tiny (<= 32x128) and the per-window working set (N=16, C=32, hidden=128) fits easily in shared memory/registers, so the kernel is overwhelmingly memory-bandwidth bound under eager execution. Goal: a fused Triton kernel (ideally a single kernel) that processes a batch of windows per program, holding weights in shared memory and intermediates in registers, to eliminate ~10 HBM roundtrips. tl.dot is used for the four matmuls; softmax is over N=16 (trivial). fp32 accumulators for LN and GEMMs; fp16 storage.
open_questions: What BLOCK_W (windows per program) gives best TC utilization vs register pressure on RTX5090 (try 2,4,8)?
Does Triton's tl.dot accept K=32 efficiently on Blackwell, or should we pad/group windows to grow M further?
Is the window-partition gather pattern (stride along W with Ww=4) coalesced when launching one program per (nH, nW) tile?
Should LN1 and LN2 use Welford or two-pass; with N*C=512 fp16 elements per window, two-pass in fp32 is cheap and stable — confirm.
Does torch.compile already fuse LN+linear or attention here on RTX5090, setting a high baseline we must beat?
Is rpe_bias broadcast across all 57600 windows identical (yes per spec) so we can preload it once per program?
Are weights stored row- or column-major after nn.Linear, and what layout maximizes tl.dot throughput (transpose at kernel start)?
Memory alignment: input tensor shape 1x720x1280x32 fp16 — last dim 32*2=64B, naturally aligned; verify strides for the reshape/permute path.
